clue.text: Alsatians disturb man committing an assault

indicators.note: to disturb something is to throw it into disorder, so the letters of the dog breed are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pack of German shepherd dogs is upset by a man who is attacking someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturb' rearranges the nine letters of ALSATIANS; the dogs look like the assailants' victims but simply supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, someone who sets upon another person violently.

clue.text: He'll take no alcohol — may get tea in bars

indicators.note: here the phrase hints that the letters of tea in bars might be got into another shape, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A teetotaller orders tea when visiting pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may get' is the anagram signal on the nine letters of TEA IN BARS; 'bars' as pubs suits the drinking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refrains from drink, so he is one who abstains.

clue.text: Go astray over good part of the Middle East

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next

parts.note: to sin is to stray from the moral path
A1 is first-class, good; the 1 is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone wanders off course above a stretch of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent; the figure 1 is read as letter I to give AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinai peninsula, between Egypt and Israel, is a region of the Middle East.

clue.text: It's assumed I filled a flighty dame with gin

indicators.note: the shuffled lady is filled with the spirit, so it goes inside her letters
a flighty person is capricious and unsettled, so the letters of dame are rearranged

parts.note: the spirit gin, taken as it is

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to plying a giddy woman with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' makes MAED, which 'filled ... with' wraps round the spirit; the definition is an adjective, imagined in the sense of supposed rather than known.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imagined is supposed or taken for granted rather than known as fact.

clue.text: First to get into dope, a top journalist was helpful

indicators.note: the abbreviation for first is placed inside the other pieces as they stand side by side

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
an editor, abbreviated ED, is a senior journalist
1st, the abbreviation, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Helping a senior reporter, the first to break into the drugs scene proves useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is the abbreviation 1ST written as IST; 'to get into' places it between ASS and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have assisted is to have helped or given aid.

clue.text: Check on Her Majesty's canopy

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a test is a check or trial
ER, Elizabetha Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: An inspection of the Queen's royal canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the abbreviation for the Queen (Elizabeth Regina). The definition is an old word: a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is the overhead frame or canopy of a four-poster bed or pulpit.

clue.text: Paid pound for a mallet

parts.note: gave, as in gave money for something
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone spent a pound on a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for a pound sterling (from libra).
explanation.definitionFit: A gavel is the small hammer an auctioneer or judge bangs to call for order.

clue.text: Commons conservationists

definitions.meaning: open grassy land shared by a village, such as village lawns
environmentalist parties and campaigners, named after their colour

explanation.definitionFit: Village greens are common land, and the Green Party and its supporters campaign for the environment.

clue.text: Mum loves ices variously presented

indicators.note: set out in different ways, so the letters of loves ices are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A mother adores ice creams served in all sorts of ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother; it means silent, as in 'keep mum'. 'variously presented' rearranges LOVES ICES.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mum is to stay silent, making no sound at all.

clue.text: Linger over large port

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece goes over, above, the next

parts.note: to lag is to linger or fall behind
OS stands for outsize, meaning large

explanation.surface: Dawdling over a big harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is the large Nigerian seaport, once that country's capital.

clue.text: Some need boots, and also light shoes

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, so the letters lie inside the run of boots, and also

explanation.surface: Some people need heavy boots, while sandals will do for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run of letters within bootS AND ALSo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandals are open, lightweight footwear held on by straps.

clue.text: Attempting to get a glimpse of the monarch

parts.note: to glimpse is to see
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A crowd member trying to catch sight of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking means trying or striving to do something.

clue.text: A Liberal — one "in another place"

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A Liberal peer sits in the House of Lords, which MPs call 'another place'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another place' is the Commons' polite name for the House of Lords, so the surface seats a Liberal there.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened.

clue.text: Back the head's strict attitude

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness; the 's is the possessive

explanation.surface: Retreat from the headmaster's rigid manner.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, a word common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternness is severity, a stiff and unbending manner.

clue.text: Vikings seem involved in their own fate

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in, inside, the fate goddess

parts.note: a Norn is one of the fate goddesses of the Vikings' own Norse mythology

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of seem are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raiders appear wrapped up in their destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' makes SEME, and 'in' places it inside one of the Norns, the three fate goddesses of Norse myth, fitting for Vikings.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen are the medieval Scandinavians, raiders and settlers of the Viking age.

clue.text: Appearing again — making entrances

indicators.note: the letters of entrances are worked into a fresh word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coming back on stage by making repeated entrances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is the anagram signal on ENTRANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or springing up anew.

clue.text: Reports coming from every direction

definitions.meaning: accounts of recent events in the papers or on air
the four compass points north, east, west and south, all directions at once

explanation.definitionFit: News is fresh information, and its letters are the abbreviations of the four compass points.

clue.text: Individual wearing a T-shirt?

parts.note: a singlet is a vest or sleeveless shirt
on, as in having clothes on

explanation.surface: A lone person dressed in a casual top?
explanation.walkthrough: A singlet is a British vest, a sleeveless undershirt, standing in for the T-shirt. Someone wearing one has a 'singlet on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single person or thing, one on its own.

clue.text: A French taste — the French put in order for it

parts.note: un is French for a
a tang is a sharp taste
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French flavour that the French tidy up for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To untangle is to unravel knots and so straighten things out.

clue.text: Liking both to write and sing music

parts.note: to pen is to write
to chant is to sing, especially a liturgical tune

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys writing and singing songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a fondness or taste for something.

clue.text: Telephone circuit

definitions.meaning: to call someone on the phone

explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a ring is to phone them, and a ring is a closed loop or round track.

clue.text: Justifiably concerned with a certain issue

parts.note: in re is Latin for in the matter of, concerning
a son is one kind of issue, or offspring

explanation.surface: A rightful worry about some particular matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a topic; here it means offspring, so a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Within reason means fairly or reasonably, within sensible limits.

clue.text: Foreign lady obliged to receive a great number

indicators.note: the first piece takes in the other, so those letters go inside it

parts.note: made, as in forced or compelled
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad compelled to welcome a huge crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' puts AM inside MADE to give MAD-AM-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French form of address for a married woman.

clue.text: Notice present and hold on

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
here, as in present and in attendance

explanation.surface: Read the notice displayed and wait.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast or cling to something.

clue.text: No good forecaster!

parts.note: read as a seer who was useless, in that nobody heeded her accurate prophecies of doom in Greek legend

explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' seems to call her a poor prophet; in the legend her predictions were right but cursed never to be believed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan princess of myth foretold disasters truly yet was ignored, so her name means an unheeded prophet.

clue.text: Honoured companion with bad cold

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
ill, as in bad or poorly

explanation.surface: A distinguished member of an order has a nasty cold.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a mild feverish cold, or simply coldness.

clue.text: Fuel containing phosphorus and resin

indicators.note: the fuel holds the element symbol inside it

parts.note: coal is a fuel
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A fuel blend with phosphorus and a sticky resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a hard tree resin used in making varnishes.

clue.text: A statue presented by a couple of Greek characters

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is another Greek letter

explanation.surface: A sculpture donated by two Greek people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people; it means letters of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a sculpture or painting of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: Giving it time, the heartless repeat

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: with its heart, the centre letter, gone, only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Given time, cruel people do it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like a description of cruel people; it removes the middle letter of THE to leave TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do something over again.

clue.text: Most sober and virtuous person, after a final home

indicators.note: the saint comes after the burial place

parts.note: a grave is a person's last resting place
ST, short for saint, a holy person

explanation.surface: A very serious good person, after being laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the usual abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravest is the superlative of grave, meaning solemn and serious.

clue.text: Turner put many articles together

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a large number
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The painter Turner assembled numerous objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J. M. W. Turner; it means a machine that turns. L is fifty in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal while it is shaped.

clue.text: The cause of some distress to the viewer

definitions.text: The cause of some distress to the viewer

parts.words: The cause of some distress to the viewer
parts.note: read as something troubling a television audience, but the distress is physical strain on the organs of sight

explanation.walkthrough: 'viewer' suggests a TV watcher upset by a programme; here it is anyone whose sight is overworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiring the vision by long reading or screen use produces aching and discomfort in the sight.
